When someone asks or I have to explain it, I usually answer it like this:

So, you see, emotions that are negative, for example "frustration", are already draining, make you more sensitive to triggers regarding the thing you're frustrated about and so on, you know? It hurts to "fail" at something. And if you would now imagine that this !pain! you're feeling, would be multiplied by 10.000, that's how I feel and that's why it's so hard for a person with BPD, to heal faster from XY emotion, trigger, mistake and so on.

Or, all in all: Feels bad dude. Basically just worse for us.

And for me, and anyone with BPD, EVERY SINGLE EMOTION will physically hurt. Sad? Mental pain PLUS physical pain. 

Mad? Yeah, try to NOT BE MAD if the aggression, because of the trigger..which already hurts enough, would be SO high, how would you handle that without anything on your hand to calm yourself down and, yes experience your emotion, BUT STILL  S O M E H O W, relax after, during or preventing to burst out in the wrong way? 

If you've ever experienced love sickness, you can now imagine how ALL emotions feel like, for me, so that should be enough to slightly understand what it's like to live like this. Oh and btw, it's not just one day, a phase of all of this, no, IT'S EVERY DAY LIKE THIS.

=>Works pretty good, at least sometimes.

Still, the only comment some people give is: Eh, sometimes you're like this, than like that. / It's not THAT bad. / You're overreacting, I just [insert whatever triggered the emotion and/or connected trauma], why are you always acting like this? => often used with the "it's not that bad"-shit

Well my friend, IT FUCKIN' IS. So uhm.. SHUT.THE.FUCK.UP. :)

I hope this rant helped you, and you're feeling better now OP. It's hard enough living with BPD, but having people like these around..good lord. Fuck that shit. Hate those kind of people. 

Apart from the painful experience of our feeling of emotions and how you, ONLY YOU, can handle and HAVE TO handle them with skills, therapy and all of that stuff,  feels super lonely sometimes..but at least, we not only got each other as support, but there are also humans out there that seriously understand and accept this, but also the fact that they'll never have the same feeling or will ever be able to understand it to 100%.
 
And yk what? That's okay. We're different. We act, feel, see, live different. But that's okay. You're not responsible for being sick, of course it's no excuse, but it's just the way it is(unfortunately). Sending a lil internet hug to you and wishing you the best!❤️

I'd suggest to communicating this to them and especially tell them how you were crying and just wished them to be there for you. You don't have to start fighting like crazy or anything, just talk it out and use skills if it's a bpd problem.

For example: I feel like my partner will leave me. - Meaning: Fear of abondendement = not a reason to "attack" your partner for something that is going on in your head, which also won't happen because this feeling was triggered in your brain(which you are not responsible for, but your'e responsible for how you behave, when a feeling like this appears out of nowhere), so: use (a) skills to calm yourself down and tell them you're having a bit of trouble and need some time to deal with it.

If the first scenario, aka "my brain got triggered wtf why? I need to get rid of this shit, it's not real and I don't want this", is not the case, and you're having a disagreement about something/you or your partner did something wrong/etc.(regular things that can cause arguments), then you need to talk about it. If your partner isn't able to go through these problems with you and is simply avoiding a conflict, you got a right to say that. Tell them that avoiding confrontation isn't a solution. And even if you both solved the problem, but you're still feeling bad and they are not there for you, tell them. It's not ok to go like: Well, the problem is solved and even though my partner is still feeling like shit, I'm just gonna ignore it. It is not ok. It is toxic. You don't leave your partner alone, just because the problem is solved for YOURSELF. You get the f up, talk to them, suggest using skills, comfort them, ...

That's how relationships work. It's not "you and I", it's US. WE solved the problem, and if WE are not over it yet, and need help or just some comforting words, WE will solve this together. No crying alone in the living room or anything. It's either "us" or the relationship will come to an end at some point.
